newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank in 800 bln yuan bank loan quota.
newsitem.headline: China central bank in 800 bln yuan bank loan quota.

text.p: China's central bank is expected to increase its quota for bank loans for 1997 to more than 800 billion yuan, the Economic Information Daily said on Tuesday.
China's four big state banks, the main banks covered by the quota system, extended a total of 793.7 billion yuan in loans in 1996, up from 638.7 billion yuan in 1995, state media has said.

The central bank, the People's Bank of China, has considered phasing out the quotas for credit and loans, a remnant of central planning, and has begun allowing some banks to lend purely on the the basis of their reserves and debt-to-equity ratio.
The higher quota for 1997 comes despite repeated statements by the central bank that it will maintain an appropriately tight monetary policy this year, after two cuts in interest rates last year.
China imposed a credit squeeze in mid-1993 to try to rein in galloping inflation.
